name: Chinese · Phrases · Work and office
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.back: Thanks for all your hard work, everyone!
entries.note: Boss to the team after a push or at day's end; also said leaving the office.

entries.back: Are you busy right now?
entries.note: Before interrupting a manager or senior colleague at their desk.

entries.back: Got it!
entries.note: The standard WeChat reply to a boss or work group message: noted, on it.

entries.back: He's in a meeting.
entries.note: Colleague or assistant explaining why someone can't come to the phone or desk.

entries.reading: wǒ xiān qù kāi gè huì
entries.back: I've got to jump into a meeting.
entries.note: Cutting a chat short with a coworker; implies you'll pick it up later.

entries.back: Time to clock out.
entries.note: Said to coworkers near quitting time, often half-joking.

entries.back: What time do you usually get off work?
entries.note: Common question between friends or coworkers, often to plan dinner.

entries.reading: wǒ jīntiān néng zǎo diǎn xiàbān ma？
entries.back: Could I leave a bit early today?
entries.note: Asking your manager; usually followed by a reason.

entries.back: Overtime again tonight.
entries.note: Complaining to a partner or coworker; the 又 carries the sigh.

entries.reading: wǒ zuìjìn máng de yūntóu zhuànxiàng
entries.back: I've been insanely busy lately.
entries.note: Literally 'busy till my head spins'. Everyday way to say you're swamped.

entries.reading: qǐng lái wǒ bàngōngshì yī tàng
entries.back: Could you come to my office for a moment?
entries.note: Manager to an employee. 一趟 means a quick trip over, not a long meeting.

entries.reading: wǒ quèrèn yīxià zài huífù nín
entries.back: Let me check and get back to you.
entries.note: To a client or superior when you don't have the answer yet.

entries.back: Did you get my email?
entries.note: Quick follow-up to a coworker, in person or on WeChat.

entries.back: The meeting's been moved to tomorrow.
entries.note: Passing on a schedule change to colleagues.

entries.back: How's your project going?
entries.note: Checking in with a colleague or team member.

entries.reading: gēn wǒ shuō yīxià jìnzhǎn ba
entries.back: Please give me a quick status update.
entries.note: Manager's line in a meeting or message; sounds businesslike.

entries.reading: zhè zhōuwǔ zhīqián néng zuò wán ma？
entries.back: Can you get it done by this Friday?
entries.note: Setting or checking a deadline with a coworker.

entries.back: Could you print this out for me?
entries.note: 麻烦 softens the request; to a colleague or admin staff.

entries.back: Nice work!
entries.note: Praise from a boss or teammate after a job well done.

entries.term: 我明天想请一天假，可以吗？
entries.reading: wǒ míngtiān xiǎng qǐng yī tiān jià，kěyǐ ma？
entries.back: Could I take tomorrow off?
entries.note: Asking your manager for a day of leave.

entries.reading: wǒ mángwán jiù guòqù zhǎo nǐmen
entries.back: I'll come find you as soon as I'm done here.
entries.note: To friends or coworkers waiting for you, e.g. before lunch or drinks.

entries.reading: zhè shì bù guī wǒ guǎn
entries.back: That's not my department.
entries.note: Deflecting a request outside your role; can sound curt.

entries.back: The boss is looking for you.
entries.note: Coworker's heads-up, often with a meaningful look.

entries.back: Does this work for you?
entries.note: Proposing a plan or draft to a client or boss and asking for approval.

entries.reading: wǒ shì xīn lái de，qǐng duō guānzhào
entries.back: I'm new here. I look forward to working with you.
entries.note: Introducing yourself on your first day; 请多关照 asks for goodwill.

entries.back: I'm working from home today.
entries.note: Telling colleagues where you are; 居家办公 is the standard term.

entries.back: Are you here on business?
entries.note: Asked of someone visiting from another city or office.

entries.back: It's always a pleasure working with you.
entries.note: Warm, slightly formal; at the end of a project or a farewell.

entries.reading: nǐ hái zài zhǎo gōngzuò ma？
entries.back: Are you still job hunting?
entries.note: Friend asking how the job search is going.

entries.reading: wǒ shàng gè yuè lízhí le
entries.back: I left the company last month.
entries.note: Neutral way to say you quit; 离职 avoids saying whether you were fired.

entries.back: I don't want to go to work tomorrow.
entries.note: The Sunday-night groan, to friends or family.
